items.prompt: White has just played the queen to e2. The black pawn on e4 attacks the knight on f3. Black to move: can that pawn capture the knight?

claims.statement: Capturing on f3 is illegal: the pawn is pinned to the king on the e-file.

hints: Look along the e-file from the white queen towards the black king.
What stands between the queen and the king, and what happens if it leaves the file?
The pawn on e4 is the only piece between them.
items.explain: The queen on e2, the pawn on e4 and the king on e8 stand on one file. A capture on f3 takes the pawn off the file and leaves the black king in check, so the rules forbid it. The knight is safe from this pawn while the pin lasts.

items.prompt: Same position, but Black's queen already stands on e7. Black to move: can the pawn on e4 capture the knight on f3 now?

claims.statement: Capturing on f3 is legal: the queen on e7 stands between the white queen and the king.

hints: Compare with the last board: one piece moved.
Is the pawn still the only piece between the white queen and the black king?
The queen on e7 now blocks the file, so the pawn is free.
items.explain: A piece on the file behind the pawn ends the pin. The capture on f3 is legal, though the queens then face each other and White may take first. This is the one change from the previous board.

items.prompt: Black has put the queen on e7, so the pawn on e4 is no longer pinned. White to move: find a move that keeps the knight safe.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: the knight move to d4 is White's best.
Engine, depth 16: the retreat to g1 is sound but at least 40 centipawns worse than d4.
Engine, depth 16: the central pawn push d4 is at least 250 centipawns worse than the best move.
Engine, depth 16: the knight jump to g5 is at least 250 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: The pawn on e4 attacks the knight and may now take it. Where can the knight go?
One tempting central pawn move leaves the knight en prise and the queens facing each other.
Move the knight to d4: it keeps the best place in the centre.
items.explain: The knight must leave f3. After d4 the pawn takes the knight, the queens meet on e2 and Black ends a piece ahead. The knight move to d4 keeps everything and is the engine's choice.

feedback_by_move.d2d4: The pawn on e4 captures the knight, the queens face each other, and Black comes out a piece ahead. The pin is gone.
feedback_by_move.f3g5: The queen on e7 takes the knight on g5 at once. Moving the knight to a square the queen attacks loses it.
feedback_by_move.f3g1: Safe, but it undoes White's development; the knight move to d4 is clearly stronger.

items.prompt: The black queen has taken the pawn on d5. Tap every white piece that is attacked and not defended.

claims.statement: The knight on d4 is the only loose white piece.

hints: Which white piece does the queen on d5 look at along the d-file?
The queen on d1 is behind the pawn on d2, so it does not reach d4.
Only the knight on d4.
items.explain: The black queen attacks the knight on d4. White's own pawn on d2 blocks the queen on d1 from defending it, so nothing guards the knight. That is why White has to move it at once.

items.prompt: White's pawn has just jumped from d2 to d4 next to the black pawn on e4. Black to move: can that pawn capture on d3 'in passing'?

claims.statement: Capturing en passant on d3 is legal here.

hints: A pawn that jumps two squares can be taken as if it had moved one.
The capture must be made at once, on the very next move.
The black pawn on e4 may land on d3.
items.explain: A pawn that advances two squares and lands beside an enemy pawn may be captured as if it had stopped one square short. The black pawn on e4 takes the pawn that stands on d4 and ends on d3.

items.prompt: The knight on f3 is attacked by the pawn on e4. Which fourth move keeps a clear edge, now that you have seen the four?

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: the queen move is White's best.
Engine, depth 16: the knight move to d4 is at least 60 centipawns worse than the queen move.
Engine, depth 16: the knight move back to g1 is at least 60 centipawns worse than the queen move.
Engine, depth 16: the knight move to e5 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the queen move.
Engine, depth 16: the bishop check on b5 is at least 250 centipawns worse than the queen move.

hints: Which move does two jobs at once: attacks the pawn and stops it capturing?
Three of the four moves move the knight; the d5 pawn then falls to the black queen.
The queen goes to e2.
items.explain: The queen move attacks the e4 pawn and pins it, so the knight is not attacked in any useful sense. Each knight move lets the queen take back the pawn on d5 with nothing lost.

feedback_by_move.f3d4: The knight is safe, but the queen takes on d5 and attacks it again. Black has its pawn back.
feedback_by_move.f3g1: A retreat that undoes White's development; the queen takes on d5 and Black is level.
feedback_by_move.f3e5: The knight sits well but the queen takes on d5 and hits it; the edge is smaller than after the queen move.
feedback_by_move.f1b5: The check can be blocked by a pawn that also attacks the bishop, and the knight on f3 is still attacked. White loses a piece.

items.prompt: White has the queen on e2 and the knight on c3 aimed at the pawn on e4; Black has only the knight on f6 behind it. Does White have more attackers of e4 than Black has defenders?

claims.statement: Two white pieces attack the pawn on e4.
One black piece defends the pawn on e4.
Engine, depth 16: taking on e4 with the knight is White's best move.

hints: List the white pieces that attack e4, then the black pieces that guard it.
A bishop on e7 does not touch e4.
Queen and knight attack it; only the knight on f6 defends it.
items.explain: Queen on e2 and knight on c3 are two attackers; the knight on f6 is the only defender. With more attackers than defenders White can take the pawn, and Black then takes back the pawn on d5.

items.prompt: Same position, but the black queen has taken the pawn on d5 and stands there. Does White have more attackers of e4 than Black has defenders?

claims.statement: Two white pieces attack the pawn on e4.
Two black pieces defend the pawn on e4.

hints: Count again for both sides: pieces and pawns.
The queen on d5 looks along the diagonal at e4.
Queen and knight attack it; knight and queen defend it. Two against two: equal.
items.explain: The queen on e2 and the knight on c3 attack e4 twice; the knight on f6 and the queen on d5 defend it twice. With equal numbers the first capture only starts a series of trades, so e4 holds.

items.prompt: Black has answered the queen move with the pawn move f5. Does a black piece now defend the pawn on e4?

claims.statement: One black piece defends the pawn on e4 (the pawn on f5).

hints: A pawn guards the two squares diagonally in front of it.
Which squares does the pawn on f5 guard from Black's side?
e4 and g4: so e4 is defended.
items.explain: A black pawn guards the squares diagonally in front of it, towards White's side. The pawn on f5 therefore guards e4 and g4, so the pawn on e4 has a defender.

items.prompt: Black has answered the queen move with the pawn move f6. Does a black piece now defend the pawn on e4?

claims.statement: No black piece defends the pawn on e4.

hints: Which squares does a black pawn on f6 guard?
Diagonally in front of it, towards White's side.
e5 and g5: not e4.
items.explain: A black pawn on f6 guards e5 and g5. The pawn on e4 is one rank further and is not guarded by it, so no black piece defends it.

items.prompt: White's knight has taken the pawn on e4. Black to move: win back the pawn on d5 with the right piece.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: knight takes d5 is Black's best reply.
Engine, depth 16: knight takes e4 is at least 120 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Two pawns are loose: the knight on e4 and the pawn on d5. Which capture keeps pieces even?
After taking the knight on e4, can White simply recapture?
Take the pawn on d5 with the knight from f6.
items.explain: The d5 pawn has no defender, so ...Nxd5 regains the pawn at no cost. Taking the knight on e4 lets the queen recapture, since the file is open, and White ends two pawns ahead.

feedback_by_move.f6e4: White's queen recaptures on e4 and the pawn on d5 is still there. Black has lost a second pawn.

items.prompt: Black has defended with the move f6, hoping to guard the pawn on e4. White to move: what is the best reply?

claims.statement: A pawn on f6 does not defend e4: no black piece defends it.
Engine, depth 16: taking the pawn on e4 with the queen, with check, is White's best.

hints: Which black piece defends the pawn on e4? Count them.
A pawn defends the squares diagonally in front of it.
Take the pawn with the queen: it comes with check.
items.explain: The pawn on f6 guards e5 and g5, not e4. The queen takes the pawn on e4 with check along the open e-file, and Black must block with the queen or bishop. White is two pawns up and keeps the initiative.

items.prompt: White has taken the e5 pawn with the knight. Black to move: name a reasonable reply.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...dxe4, ...Bd6 and ...Nf6 are Black's best three replies, within 60 centipawns of each other.

hints: The knight on e5 is attacked by nothing yet. Which Black move makes it a target or opens the d-file?
One reply takes a pawn, one attacks the knight with a bishop, one develops.
Try ...dxe4, ...Bd6 or ...Nf6.
items.explain: These replies fight for the knight on e5 or open lines for Black. The engine puts White somewhat ahead after either, so Black is paying for activity, not winning material.

items.prompt: White has played the bishop to c4 on move three. Black to move: win material.

claims.statement: The pawn on d5 attacks the bishop on c4.
Taking the bishop wins at least two pawns' worth of material for Black.
Engine, depth 16: taking the bishop is Black's best move.

hints: Which black piece attacks the bishop on c4?
Is the bishop defended?
Take it with the d-pawn.
items.explain: The pawn on d5 attacks the bishop on c4, and no white piece defends it. Black wins a bishop for nothing.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...Qxd5 is Black's best.
Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the best move.
Engine, depth 16: ...c6 is at least 50 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Look at the pawn White took on move three.
Is it defended?
Take it with the queen.
items.explain: The pawn on d5 has no defender and the queen takes it, regaining the pawn. The queen on d5 also attacks the knight on d4, whose only guard is blocked by White's own pawn.

feedback_by_move.g8f6: Develops, but the d5 pawn stays with White and the position is no longer level.
feedback_by_move.c7c6: Offers a pawn trade instead of regaining the first pawn; White keeps the extra pawn.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...Qxd5 is Black's best.
Engine, depth 16: ...Bb4+ is at least 60 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Which Black pieces defend the pawn on e4, and how many attack it?
The pawn on e4 cannot take on d3.
Take on d5 with the queen: it adds a defender.
items.explain: White now attacks e4 twice, with the d3 pawn and the queen, and the pinned e4 pawn cannot capture. The queen takes the pawn on d5, which regains material and adds a second defender of e4.

feedback_by_move.f8b4: The check wins nothing: it is blocked with tempo, and the pawn on d5 is still White's.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: ...Nf6 and ...Qe7 are Black's best, within 40 centipawns of each other.
Engine, depth 16: ...f6 is at least 250 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Count who defends e4 after each candidate.
A pawn defends diagonally.
Develop with ...Nf6 or interpose with ...Qe7.
items.explain: Both moves keep material and deal with the attack on e4: the knight defends the pawn and attacks d5, the queen interposes and ends the pin. The tempting ...f6 does not defend e4 at all.

feedback_by_move.f7f6: The pawn on f6 does not guard e4. The queen takes it with check and Black is two pawns down.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a good move.

claims.statement: Engine, depth 16: Nb5, Nb3 and Ne2 are all good, within 40 centipawns of the best.
Engine, depth 16: c3 is at least 40 centipawns worse than the best move.

hints: Is any white piece attacked and undefended?
The knight on d4 is loose.
Move it to b5, b3 or e2.
items.explain: The black queen attacks the knight on d4. A pawn move to c3 does protect it, but the knight stays on d4 where Black keeps hitting it and gains time, about six tenths of a pawn. Any of the three knight moves saves it with more.

feedback_by_move.c2c3: c3 does defend the knight, but it leaves it on d4 where Black keeps attacking it and gains time; the engine prefers moving the knight.
